rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-year field experiment (2014, 2015) in the North China Plain with three dripline depths (0, 15, 30 cm) and three irrigation levels, randomized complete block, sewage effluent and groundwater controls. Q2: Results 'Nitrate leaching', Table 4 and Conclusions <U+2013> cumulative NO3<U+2013>N leaching at a given irrigation level generally increased as lateral depth increased (e.g. I1D3 189% and 86% higher than I1D1 and I1D2 in 2014, lateral depth significant at P=0.062); Table 5 and Conclusions <U+2013> sewage effluent irrigation gave higher cumulative NO3<U+2013>N leaching than groundwater (e.g. 54 vs 13 kg/ha at 15 cm depth in 2015), significant in 2014 (P=0.100). Q4: Tables 4 and 6, 'Deep percolation' and 'Nitrate leaching' sections <U+2013> the study measured deep percolation at 70 cm (tensiometer pairs with K(h)) and NO3<U+2013>N concentration in leachate (suction cups), showing deeper driplines produced greater deep percolation (e.g. I3D3 78% and 13% higher than I3D1) and higher leachate NO3<U+2013>N concentration (23.2, 27.2, 36.2 mg/L for D1, D2, D3 at I1 in 2015), the intermediate variables through which lateral depth increases leaching. Q8: 'Nitrate leaching' section <U+2013> authors state that spatial variability of soil physical<U+2013>chemical properties could produce variability in leachate NO3<U+2013>N concentration and deep percolation, dampening the detected influence of irrigation parameters on leaching, and that heavy rainfall in the semi-humid region compensated for treatment differences; results are qualified as holding 'under our field conditions'.
rows.notes: Leaching estimated by a single method (tensiometer-derived flux times suction-cup concentration) in one replicate per treatment, so no triangulation and no replicate dispersion for cumulative leaching (Table 6 SDs are temporal variation of leachate concentration, not dispersion of the seasonal leaching result; Table 4 significance only by Tukey P-values). Single site, single crop (maize), single silt loam soil, plot scale. Q7 doubtful: authors state intensive rainfall was the driving force of leaching and recommend a 15 cm dripline with deficit irrigation, but do not frame a condition as a requirement for the lateral-depth effect, so answered no. Lateral depth effect was significant only in 2014, not in 2015.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is on subsurface drip irrigation with secondary sewage effluent (TSE) and groundwater on maize in Beijing; claim concerns nitrate leaching to below the root zone (groundwater contamination risk), which the study measured directly.
